120	# Temporal Rust SDK (Public Preview; crates.io since 2026-02-19). TLS risk (requires
121	# verification on every temporalio-* bump): temporalio-common CAN pull a second
122	# reqwest + TLS stack via opentelemetry-otlp, but only behind its `otel` feature —
123	# both `opentelemetry-otlp` and `reqwest` are `optional = true` there, and
124	# `tls-aws-lc` names opentelemetry-otlp only *weakly* (`opentelemetry-otlp?/…`), so
125	# it does not activate it. Nothing in this workspace enables `otel`, and the lock
126	# carries exactly one reqwest. The standing risk this comment guards is therefore a
127	# FUTURE feature flip enabling `otel`, not a present-day second stack. (Corrected in
128	# SMA-622: the previous wording claimed an *unconditional* pull of reqwest 0.12 via
129	# hyper-rustls. That was never true — not at 0.7.0 either — and re-verifying against
130	# a fiction is worse than having no comment.)
131	# Safety still rests on all consumers unifying on the single shared rustls 0.23
132	# instance, which resolves to aws-lc-rs for every consumer — verify with
133	# `cargo tree -i ring --all-features -e normal --target all`, which must print
134	# "nothing to print". Use `--target all`: cargo otherwise resolves for the host only,
135	# and temporalio-client 1.0.0 carries a non-optional tokio-rustls plus an optional
136	# rustls-native-certs — exactly the deps most likely to be platform-gated.
137	# The `-e normal` is load-bearing: plain `cargo tree -i ring` DOES report a hit via
138	# `rcgen`, a dev-dependency of paigasus-helikon-tools that has nothing to do with the
139	# TLS stack. Only a *normal* dependency on ring would mean a second CryptoProvider.
140	# The `ephemeral-server` feature (temporalio-sdk-core) additionally pulls its own
141	# reqwest+TLS stack and must stay unenabled; runtime-temporal's integration tests use
142	# the external-server env gate instead.
143	# temporalio-sdk-core is a direct dep that NO source file names (`rg
144	# temporalio_sdk_core crates/` is empty); it exists solely to force `tls-aws-lc`
145	# through feature unification. Do not "clean it up".
146	# `vendored-protox` (SMA-623): temporalio-protos and prost-wkt-types compile their
147	# .proto files with `protox` (pure Rust) instead of a system `protoc`, so neither
148	# this workspace nor its downstream users need protoc. The feature must stay on
149	# temporalio-client (or temporalio-common): temporalio-sdk and temporalio-sdk-core
150	# do not forward it. protox and its dependencies are BUILD dependencies, so the
151	# `-e normal` ring check above does not see them. Two ci.yml guards fail the
152	# required gates if the feature disappears: a `cargo tree` assertion in
153	# `build-no-default-features`, and `PROTOC` set to a path that does not exist.
154	temporalio-sdk      = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
155	temporalio-client   = { version = "1.0", default-features = false, features = ["tls-aws-lc", "vendored-protox"] }
156	temporalio-sdk-core = { version = "0.9", default-features = false, features = ["tls-aws-lc"] }
157	temporalio-common   = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
158	# temporalio-sdk does NOT re-export the `#[activities]`/`#[activity]` attribute
159	# macros (verified by reading temporalio-sdk-1.0.0/src/lib.rs: its own doctest
160	# imports them from `temporalio_macros` directly) — a direct dependency is
161	# required to invoke them, even though temporalio-macros was already pulled in
162	# transitively as a proc-macro dep of temporalio-sdk/temporalio-workflow.
163	temporalio-macros   = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }
164	# temporalio-workflow: the `#[workflow]`/`#[workflow_methods]` macro-generated
165	# code references `::temporalio_workflow::…` (verified in
166	# temporalio-macros-1.0.0/src/workflow_definitions.rs), and it exports the
167	# workflow-authoring types (`WorkflowContext`, `ActivityOptions`, `join_all`,
168	# `select!`, …) that `temporalio-sdk` re-exports. A direct dependency is
169	# required to invoke the workflow macros, mirroring the temporalio-macros note
170	# above.
171	temporalio-workflow = { version = "1.0", default-features = false }

173	# AWS SDK — rustls + aws-lc-rs TLS connector.
174	# aws-config "default-https-client" → aws-smithy-runtime/default-https-client
175	# → aws-smithy-http-client/rustls-aws-lc (rustls 0.23 + aws-lc-rs).
176	# This shares the aws-lc-rs CryptoProvider already registered by

1	[package]
2	name        = "paigasus-helikon"
3	description = "Paigasus AI SDK — facade crate. Re-exports core plus feature-gated providers and runtimes."
4	version                = "0.7.0"
5	edition.workspace      = true
6	rust-version.workspace = true
7	authors.workspace      = true
8	license.workspace      = true
9	repository.workspace   = true
10	homepage.workspace     = true
11	keywords.workspace     = true
12	categories.workspace   = true
13	
14	[dependencies]
15	paigasus-helikon-core                = { workspace = true }
16	paigasus-helikon-macros              = { workspace = true, optional = true }
17	paigasus-helikon-providers-openai    = { workspace = true, optional = true }
18	paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic = { workspace = true, optional = true }
19	paigasus-helikon-mcp                 = { workspace = true, optional = true }
20	paigasus-helikon-tools               = { workspace = true, optional = true }
21	paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio       = { workspace = true, optional = true }
22	paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum        = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["openapi"] }
23	paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix       = { workspace = true, optional = true, features = ["openapi"] }
24	paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal    = { workspace = true, optional = true }
25	paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore   = { workspace = true, optional = true }
26	paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite     = { workspace = true, optional = true }
27	paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres   = { workspace = true, optional = true }
28	paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis      = { workspace = true, optional = true }
29	paigasus-helikon-evals               = { workspace = true, optional = true }
30	paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock   = { workspace = true, optional = true }
31	paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini    = { workspace = true, optional = true }
32	paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm   = { workspace = true, optional = true }
33	
34	[features]
35	default            = []
36	macros             = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-macros"]
37	openai             = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-openai"]
38	providers-openai   = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-openai"]
39	anthropic          = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-anthropic"]
40	mcp                = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-mcp"]
41	tools              = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-tools"]
42	tools-web          = ["tools", "paigasus-helikon-tools/web"]
43	tools-os-sandbox   = ["tools", "paigasus-helikon-tools/os-sandbox"]
44	tools-microvm      = ["tools", "paigasus-helikon-tools/microvm"]
45	evals              = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-evals"]
46	runtime-tokio      = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-runtime-tokio"]
47	runtime-axum       = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-runtime-axum"]
48	runtime-actix      = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-runtime-actix"]
49	runtime-temporal   = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-runtime-temporal"]
50	runtime-agentcore  = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-runtime-agentcore"]
51	sessions-sqlite    = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite"]
52	sessions-postgres  = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres"]
53	sessions-redis     = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-sessions-redis"]
54	bedrock            = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-bedrock"]
55	gemini             = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-gemini"]
56	litellm            = ["dep:paigasus-helikon-providers-litellm"]
57	
58	[dev-dependencies]
59	# Installs git hooks from .cargo-husky/hooks/ when this crate's
60	# dev-deps are realized (e.g. `cargo test -p paigasus-helikon --no-run`).
61	# See SMA-335 design doc §4.
62	cargo-husky = { version = "1", default-features = false, features = ["user-hooks"] }
63	# Trybuild for the facade_only_consumer UI test (SMA-385 §5.5 — moved
64	# here from paigasus-helikon-macros to break the publish-time dep cycle).
65	# serde_json is required because the #[tool] macro expansion emits
66	# `::serde_json::…` paths directly (see -macros/src/expand.rs).
67	trybuild    = { workspace = true }
68	schemars    = { workspace = true }
69	serde       = { workspace = true }
70	serde_json  = { workspace = true }
71	# Required by the structured_output example (SMA-323).
72	tokio       = { workspace = true, features = ["macros", "rt-multi-thread"] }
73	anyhow      = { workspace = true }
74	# SMA-322 — OTel export stack for the langfuse_tracing example + otel_spans test.
75	async-trait           = { workspace = true }
76	futures-core          = { workspace = true }
77	futures-util          = { workspace = true }
78	tracing               = { workspace = true }
79	tracing-subscriber    = { workspace = true }
80	tracing-opentelemetry = { workspace = true }
81	opentelemetry         = { workspace = true }
82	opentelemetry_sdk     = { workspace = true }
83	opentelemetry-otlp    = { workspace = true }
84	base64                = { workspace = true }
85	# Required by the openai_litellm_message_parity cross-crate test (SMA-451).
86	wiremock              = { workspace = true }
87	
88	[[example]]
89	name              = "structured_output"
90	required-features = ["anthropic"]
91	
92	[[example]]
93	name              = "budget_assistant_openai"
94	required-features = ["openai", "macros"]
95	
96	[[example]]
97	name              = "budget_assistant_anthropic"
98	required-features = ["anthropic", "macros"]
99	
100	[[example]]
101	name              = "streaming_console"
102	required-features = ["openai"]
103	
104	[[example]]
105	name              = "langfuse_tracing"
106	required-features = ["runtime-tokio"]
107	
108	[[example]]
109	name              = "multi_agent_triage"
110	required-features = ["openai"]
111	
112	[[example]]
113	name              = "swarm_finance"
114	required-features = ["openai"]
115	
116	[[example]]
117	name              = "graph_report"
118	required-features = ["openai"]
119	
120	[[bench]]
121	name    = "tool_dispatch"
122	harness = false
123	# A benchmark, not a test: `test = false` keeps `cargo test` from building and
124	# running the timing loop, and keeps it out of the `test (…, 1.85)` CI job.
125	test    = false
126	
127	[lints]
128	workspace = true

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.7.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-v0.6.14...paigasus-helikon-v0.7.0) - 2026-11-20

### Other

- *(deps)* [**breaking**] SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 ([#367](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/367))

### Upgrade notes

- This release requires `jiff` 1. The `ts` fields of `SessionEvent` and the return value of `SessionEvent::ts()` now have the type `jiff::Timestamp` from jiff 1. A `Timestamp` from jiff 0.2 is a different type.
- If your code passes a `Timestamp` into a `SessionEvent`, or uses the value from `ts()` with jiff code, change your `jiff` requirement to `1`. Read the [jiff 1.0 changelog](https://github.com/BurntSushi/jiff/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for the APIs that jiff renamed.
- If your code uses only the constructors that set `ts` to the current time (for example `SessionEvent::user_message`) and does not read `ts`, it needs no change.
- Upgrade `paigasus-helikon-core` and `paigasus-helikon` to 0.7 together.
- The next patch release of each other `paigasus-helikon-*` crate requires core 0.7. If your `Cargo.toml` requires `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6 directly, change it to `0.7` before you run `cargo update`. If you cannot upgrade core yet, keep the other `paigasus-helikon-*` crates at their current versions with `cargo update --precise`. Two copies of core in one build cause errors such as "trait not implemented". Run `cargo tree -d` to find the copies.
- The JSON format of a stored `SessionEvent` does not change. Session rows that an earlier version wrote stay readable.

## [0.6.14](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-v0.6.13...paigasus-helikon-v0.6.14) - 2026-11-20

### Other

- updated the following local packages: paigasus-helikon-evals, paigasus-helikon-sessions-postgres, paigasus-helikon-sessions-sqlite

1	# Changelog
2	
3	All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.
4	
5	The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
6	and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).
7	
8	## [Unreleased]
9	
10	## [0.7.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.6.0...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.7.0) - 2026-11-20
11	
12	### Fixed
13	
14	- *(core)* SMA-810 give each handoff transfer call a tool result ([#358](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/358))
15	
16	### Other
17	
18	- *(deps)* [**breaking**] SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 ([#367](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/367))
19	- *(core)* SMA-828 share the deferral test helpers with runtime-tokio ([#366](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/366))
20	- *(core)* SMA-826 move the shared core test helpers into tests/common ([#359](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/359))
21	
22	### Upgrade notes

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## [Unreleased]

## [0.7.0](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/compare/paigasus-helikon-core-v0.6.0...paigasus-helikon-core-v0.7.0) - 2026-11-20

### Fixed

- *(core)* SMA-810 give each handoff transfer call a tool result ([#358](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/358))

### Other

- *(deps)* [**breaking**] SMA-831 upgrade jiff to 1 ([#367](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/367))
- *(core)* SMA-828 share the deferral test helpers with runtime-tokio ([#366](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/366))
- *(core)* SMA-826 move the shared core test helpers into tests/common ([#359](https://github.com/SMK1085/paigasus-helikon/pull/359))

### Upgrade notes

- This release requires `jiff` 1. The `ts` fields of `SessionEvent` and the return value of `SessionEvent::ts()` now have the type `jiff::Timestamp` from jiff 1. A `Timestamp` from jiff 0.2 is a different type.
- If your code passes a `Timestamp` into a `SessionEvent`, or uses the value from `ts()` with jiff code, change your `jiff` requirement to `1`. Read the [jiff 1.0 changelog](https://github.com/BurntSushi/jiff/blob/master/CHANGELOG.md) for the APIs that jiff renamed.
- If your code uses only the constructors that set `ts` to the current time (for example `SessionEvent::user_message`) and does not read `ts`, it needs no change.
- Upgrade `paigasus-helikon-core` and `paigasus-helikon` to 0.7 together.
- The next patch release of each other `paigasus-helikon-*` crate requires core 0.7. If your `Cargo.toml` requires `paigasus-helikon-core` 0.6 directly, change it to `0.7` before you run `cargo update`. If you cannot upgrade core yet, keep the other `paigasus-helikon-*` crates at their current versions with `cargo update --precise`. Two copies of core in one build cause errors such as "trait not implemented". Run `cargo tree -d` to find the copies.
- The JSON format of a stored `SessionEvent` does not change. Session rows that an earlier version wrote stay readable.

## Verdict: APPROVE WITH CHANGES
The repair is sound. The version table matches every `crates/*/Cargo.toml:4`. All sibling dev-deps are path-only (core:34,38; runtime-tokio:31; sessions-*:22-25; tools:51), so there is no publish-time cycle. The runbook precedent (`release-ascend.md:36,40`) shows that a hand bump gets a dependency-ordered publish on its own merge. The guard has three problems: a scope hole that this incident class already fell through once, a base revision that can change between runs, and a route to a vacuous pass.

## Findings

### BLOCKER
None.

### MAJOR
- **The core-only guard misses the facade cascade.** On 2026-08-14, runtime-temporal went from 0.3.1 to 0.4.0 (`runtime-temporal/CHANGELOG.md:124`). On the same day the facade went from 0.5.2 to 0.5.3 (`paigasus-helikon/CHANGELOG.md:247-251`). That is a patch that re-exports a breaking sibling. The same class applies to runtime-tokio → axum/actix/agentcore/evals and to runtime-axum/mcp → agentcore. | Why it matters: the guard reads versions, so it would also catch breaks that cargo-semver-checks infers, but only for core. | Suggested fix: make the rule general: "any publishable crate with a breaking bump ⇒ every non-exempt normal dependent gets a breaking bump". Land it in a follow-up PR after the repair publishes, so its base and head versions are equal. Or exempt only facade 0.7.1.
- **The base revision changes between runs.** The step fetches the tip of `main` at job time. But the checkout is `refs/pull/N/merge`, which GitHub built against `main` at event time. A re-run keeps the old merge SHA and fetches a newer `main`. If a release merged in between, the diff shows versions that go down, and the spec counts any change of `y` as breaking. | Suggested fix: set `fetch-depth: 2` and use base = `HEAD^1`. This needs no network and works on forks. Define "breaking" as an increase. Make a decrease fail loudly with its own message.
- **Vacuous-pass and false-block routes.** (a) Exit 0 only when `GITHUB_EVENT_NAME == push`. Any other event, or a missing base, must fail. Define the base for local runs (the merge-base with `origin/main`). (b) Skip a crate that is absent at base (a new crate). Otherwise the "unreadable base" rule blocks every PR that adds a crate. Add both cases to the self-test.
- **A book pin breaks after the yank.** `docs/book/src/concepts/model-providers.md:282` has `providers-gemini = { version = "0.1" }`. After the yank, that resolves to 0.1.10, which uses core 0.6. Lines `:402-410` still say facade `"0.5"`. | Suggested fix: change them to `"0.2"` and `"0.7"`, and add the book to "Changes" (the CLAUDE.md book rule applies). I found no other sibling `version =` pin in `crates/`, the READMEs or the examples.
- **Published upgrade notes become wrong, and the obvious fix for core is a trap.** `core/CHANGELOG.md:28` and `paigasus-helikon/CHANGELOG.md:22` say "the next patch release of each other crate requires core 0.7". | Suggested fix: correct the facade 0.7.0 note in place, because the facade republishes anyway. For core, edit only the body of the `paigasus-helikon-core-v0.7.0` GitHub release. State that the repair PR must not touch any file in core or macros. release-plz compares each package with the registry copy, and Approach A depends on this. So any edit there opens a release PR for core 0.7.1, which gives patch bumps to all 19 crates.

### MINOR
- **CLI 0.1.44 can only be installed with `--locked` after the yank.** It does not depend on the facade. `cli/Cargo.toml:25-29` requires evals ^0.1.22, runtime-tokio ^0.1.27, openai ^0.2.34, anthropic ^0.1.29 and mcp ^0.1.26. Only yanked versions satisfy these requirements. Yank 0.1.44 too, or document this.
- **Users who already moved to core 0.7.** After the yank, `cargo update` silently moves a `"0.1"` requirement back to the core-0.6 build. This gives the same two-cores error, with no resolver error. The CHANGELOG text must tell these users to change the requirement to the new minor.
- **`dependencies_update` is also described as a cascade** in `release-ascend.md:40` and in `CLAUDE.md`. Correct all three places, not only `release-plz.toml:5-9`.
- **Partial publish.** Write in the release sequence: do not yank until all 19 versions are on crates.io. If the run fails part way, re-run it; release-plz skips versions that are already published.
- `ci.yml:56-67` runs one guard and two self-tests, not three guards.

### QUESTIONS
- Facade 0.7.1 changes the identity of every re-exported type (for example openai 0.2 becomes 0.3). Do you accept this only because 0.7.0 is yanked? If so, say it in the facade CHANGELOG.
- Which command proves that release-plz publishes the 19 versions and bumps nothing further? A `release-plz update` before the merge cannot see the registry as it is after the publish. I suggest `release-plz release --dry-run` for the publish list and order. After the merge, also check that no release PR opens.

## What's good
- "Publish first, yank second" keeps each local version off a yanked version, so release-plz#524 does not apply.
- The guard reads versions, not commit types, so it also catches a break that cargo-semver-checks infers. The checks ruleset has no bypass actors (`main-protection-checks.json:11`), so a red `fmt` on the release PR stops the publish even with `--admin`. The bot pushes with its App token, so each new version of the release PR runs `fmt` again.
- The hand bump covers every crate that depends on a bumped crate.

## What's good
- "Publish first, yank second" keeps each local version off a yanked version, so release-plz#524 does not apply.
- The guard reads versions, not commit types, so it also catches a break that cargo-semver-checks infers. The checks ruleset has no bypass actors (`main-protection-checks.json:11`), so a red `fmt` on the release PR stops the publish even with `--admin`. The bot pushes with its App token, so each new version of the release PR runs `fmt` again.
- The hand bump covers every crate that depends on a bumped crate.
